## Install the panel

```sh
# npm (recommended, no build step required)
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-armory

# From GitHub
dsh plugin --profile web add github:2026heshao/dsh-armory
```

After installing, **fully quit DSH and then restart it**. A new row, Dafeiyu Armory (大肥鱼军械库), appears in the top-left corner under the Global Panel. Click it to open. The floating button in the bottom-right corner and the bottom of the left sidebar also open it. On desktop, replace `--profile web` with `--profile desktop`.

You can keep just one of the three entry points or enable all of them. Switch them in the Entry menu at the top-right of the panel. You can't end up with all three disabled and no way to open it.

> Don't manually insert `dsh-armory` into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, an Agent preset, or an extra `--patch` file. The plugin command already handles this, and duplicate wiring will raise an explicit error.

## What it keeps an eye on for you

### MCP: see at a glance whether it's connected

Each MCP gets one row showing its status, transport, connection parameters, and tool count. Expand it to see the full input schema, including required and optional fields, enums, and defaults. Credentials are masked by default; click to reveal them temporarily, and click again to hide them. If a connection fails, reconnect in place without restarting the host.

Global and project scopes are managed separately. Global settings are written to the profile and available to all projects. Project settings are written to `.dsh/mcp.json` and visible only to sessions in that project. Within a project you can also block a given global MCP without affecting other projects. Migrating from other clients doesn't require copying entries one by one. Configs from 11 clients, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI, and Roo Code, are detected automatically. Preview them and import with one click. On name conflicts, only the conflicting entry is skipped. Pasting `mcpServers` JSON also works.

For remote MCPs that require OAuth, a 401 response from the server opens the authorization dialog directly. The browser completes discovery, registration, PKCE, and the callback. The token is written back to the config, and the plugin refreshes it before it expires. If the callback isn't received, you can paste the callback URL or an access token.

### Tool tailor: who's consuming tokens

Each MCP's tool descriptions are sent into the context with every request. Tools with zero calls do no work but still take up space.

# nihongo

## Prohibited uses

Do not use this for fraud, phishing, impersonation, or sentences intended to deceive others. It is also prohibited under the terms of use of each AI service, such as Claude and ChatGPT.

nihongo values not deceiving readers. It does not write reasons, promises, or numbers that were not requested, and it does not misrepresent the sender.

## What is nihongo

### nihongo — A Japanese guard for AI editing

It eliminates “good work, but can't be sent as is.” It takes on the finishing and checking of AI edits in one go.

Japanese written by AI may look clean at first glance, yet the honorific level may be one step too high, promises nobody asked for may creep in, and dates, times, or “必ず” (“certainly”) may get dropped during revision. nihongo v3.0 is a mechanism that **on the first day reduces common mismatches that nearly everyone tends to run into, and as you keep using it, learns your own writing habits and expressions to avoid one line at a time, reducing the amount of rework.** It divides the finishing and checking work among the following three parts.

- **Lightweight skill (Lite / Full)**: For everyday exchanges, the short Lite (about 1,200 characters) is used, while emails, documents, and technical writing are handled by Full (about 93 lines plus 21 detailed reference documents). It does not add facts or promises that were not requested, and it shapes the Japanese to suit the recipient and the situation.
- **Personal, which grows through conversation**: Your writing habits are saved in `~/.nihongo/profile.md`, divided into four boxes (`[common]` / `[casual]` / `[work]` / `[formal]`) and a list of expressions you never want to say. Only habits corrected in conversation are added, after a one-line confirmation, and it never silently rewrites the file in the background.
- **Zero-token automatic checker (`nihongo-check`)**: A CLI that runs on only the Python 3.10+ standard library. It compares the original text with the edited text and, at zero token cost, finds **candidates for review**: mismatches in dates, times, numbers, negation, conditions, and requested strength (such as “必ず”), as well as unwanted expressions. It can also be dropped straight into Claude Code Hooks or GitHub Actions.

## Try it first

**Everyday ChatGPT / Claude (web and app, no command needed)**

1. Open [nihongo/WEB.md](https://github.com/AnIT012/nihongo/blob/HEAD/nihongo/WEB.md) and click the copy button in the upper right.
2. Paste it as-is into “Custom instructions (ChatGPT)” or “Response preferences (Claude)” in the settings screen, and save.

Everyday users can get started with just this. (The CLI, Hook, and MCP below are additional features for those who want to automate further in a development environment.)

# remedy — ESTsecurity dedicated antivirus

A dedicated antivirus that runs without installation and can **find, remediate, and revert** specific threats. Used on Windows · Linux.

- **Shows before changing** — Scanning changes nothing. Remediation shows everything it will change and starts only after you approve.
- **Reversible** — Deleted files are quarantined and can be restored with the menu item *Restore to before remediation*.
- **No communication** — The scan and remediation executables have no network features, so they work on air-gapped networks. The *Remote check* item, which uses the network, is handled by the separately included `remedy-net`, and you are notified before you choose it.
- **Uses only signed rules** — Rule signatures are verified with the public key built into the executable.

## Quick start

1. **Download** — From [latest version](https://github.com/ESTsecurity/remedy/releases/latest), download one file for your platform.
   One file contains the program and the rules for that OS.

   | Platform | File to download |

   | Linux x86_64 — RHEL family · Debian · Ubuntu · Alpine | `remedy-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

流声音乐 (CurrentMusicX) is the native Android client for [CurrentMusic](https://github.com/backrooms-yrc/CurrentMusic). The app's Chinese display name is 流声音乐, while its English name remains CurrentMusic. Circular covers, dynamic color extraction, word-by-word lyrics, and a floating player connect the music library, discovery, and playback smoothly, and the app adapts to portrait, landscape, and widescreen layouts.

## Interface Preview

## 开始使用

1. **Download and install.** Go to [Releases](https://github.com/bileizhen/CurrentMusicX/releases/latest) and download `CurrentMusic-Android-v版本号.apk`, then install it by following the system prompts. Official releases signed with the same key can be installed over the existing version as an upgrade.
2. **Choose sources.** In 'Settings → Audio Source & Network', select the music source and the lyrics source separately. Lyrics default to **auto-select best: word-by-word first, line-by-line as fallback**.
3. **Connect a music library.** As needed, log in to CurrentMusic, bind NetEase Cloud Music, or tap **Current Music** in the top left to switch and scan a QR code to log in to QQ Music. You can also connect Navidrome / Emby under 'Settings → Audio Source & Network → Self-hosted Library' to search, favorite, and play music. Connected library entries appear under 'Me → Music Services' and are hidden after you log out.

Availability of songs, audio quality, member sound effects, and recommendations depends on the corresponding service and account permissions. This page describes the current `main` source code. jon890/dooray-cli.body:
# dooray-cli

[NHN Dooray](https://dooray.com) is a CLI that lets you use Dooray from the terminal and AI agents.

Handle tasks, comments, wiki, mail, messenger, and calendar with single command lines.
Install it as a skill in Claude Code and Codex, and it understands requests like "create a task" and handles them.

```
"Create a task '로그인 실패 로그 확인' in the 백엔드 project and assign it to 김철수"
"Add a comment '80% 완료' to task 42"
"Show me unread mail"
"Notify the 개발팀 chat room that the deployment is complete"
```

## This is for you if

- You want to check and organize Dooray tasks in the terminal without opening the Dooray web app
- You want to have an AI agent handle task creation, comments, and wiki organization
- You want to automate repetitive Dooray work, such as deployment alerts or regular reports, with scripts

## Quick start

Node.js 20 or later is required.

### 1. Install

```bash
npm install -g @bifos/dooray-cli
```

In a repository that pins Node.js with mise, install with `mise use -g npm:@bifos/dooray-cli`.
The `dooray` shim installed with `npm install -g` fails in that repository with `No version is set for shim: dooray`.

### 2. Connect your Dooray account

For the API key method, create a token in Dooray web under **설정 → API → 인증 토큰**.
If you cannot use an API key, choose `web` in setup to connect using the SESSION cookie from your web login session.
Then run the command below, and it will ask you for the required values one by one.

```bash
dooray setup
```

Check that the connection works with `doctor`.

```bash
dooray doctor
```

# Running Assistant

## Project Introduction

Running Assistant is a campus running Web application based on Python Flask. It provides a unified Web-based entry point and supporting capabilities around campus running task scenarios. The capabilities clearly visible in the current code include: account and session management, automatic check-in configuration, payment order processing, health checks, Nginx log forwarding, theme and random background handling, and payment product name generation.

- Tech stack: Python, Flask, Flask-SocketIO, Playwright, Nginx
- Live site: http://run.zelly.cn

## Features

- Provides a Web-based management entry point for campus running scenarios
- On first startup with a new database, initializes configuration, permissions, and the default administrator account
- Supports automatic check-in configuration and session persistence
- Supports payment order status transitions, QR code caching, and payment method configuration
- Provides `/health` health checks and Nginx access log forwarding
- Supports theme styles and random background caching
- Built-in payment product name generator, currently registered with `lomei` and `travel_service` modes

## Database Storage

By default, a SQLite database `data/application.sqlite3` is created for local development and testing, and external MySQL/MariaDB can also be connected. The file-based backend is frozen and rejected at runtime. Structured data such as accounts, sessions, tokens, orders, bills, main configuration, and trusted IPs is stored in separate tables by domain. Core typed columns are the authoritative source, and multi-account UAs are isolated by user binding. Log locations and mounts are unchanged; images, uploads, caches, and certificates continue to be kept at their original disk paths.

Legacy data must be imported offline, after writes are stopped, using `--backend sqlite` or `--backend mysql` of `tools/migrate_storage.py`, and then verified independently. Exports can be used for backup or re-import into a database; restoring to the file backend is not supported. Compose configures connection variables directly under `environment` and does not use env files. `run/docker-compose.mysql.yml` only connects to an external database and does not bundle MySQL. Mounts of the old managed directory have been removed; migration requires separately mounting the complete source directory read-only. This version only supports a single application instance. For operations and test tools, see [Database Storage and Offline Migration](https://github.com/liu2-3zhi/Campus-Running-Assistant-For-ZSC/blob/HEAD/docs/mysql-storage.md), and for the structure description, see [Database-First Storage Design](https://github.com/liu2-3zhi/Campus-Running-Assistant-For-ZSC/blob/HEAD/docs/database-first-design.md).

# CarDeck — Let an Android phone connect to a car head unit like an iPhone

Make an ordinary Android phone (not rooted) act as the **CarPlay sender (iPhone role)**,
projecting the app's self-drawn interface onto a head unit that supports CarPlay.

> **Unofficial project**: This project is a personal experimental work. It is not affiliated with Apple Inc. or any automaker,
> is not authorized or certified, and **is not an MFi product**. CarPlay / AirPlay are trademarks of Apple Inc.; they appear in the text only to describe compatible targets.
>
> **Driving safety**: Configure and operate only while parked. Disconnecting while driving may interrupt navigation; please use the factory navigation as a safety backup.
>
> For the full terms, see [DISCLAIMER.md](https://github.com/shaonialife/cardeck/blob/HEAD/DISCLAIMER.md) (same source as the disclaimer shown on the app's first launch).

## Conclusion first (feasibility)

- **Direction is opposite to DiPlay/xcertplay**: they are receivers (head-unit role); this project is the sender.
  **DiPlay is a derivative of xcertplay and is also the test bench actually used by this project**; the source code of both in `reference/` is kept for reference (protocol knowledge is shared at the iAP2/link layer/Bonjour layer, while role logic is not shared between them).
- **The sender does not need an Apple signing identity**: iAP2 authentication is one-way (the phone verifies the head unit's MFi certificate, and the head unit trusts the phone's self-reported result; publicly confirmed by Oligo Security at DEF CON 2025).
- **The wired USB route has been ruled out** (the app cannot control the USB gadget, and Honor devices cannot unlock the BL), so only the wireless route is used: Bluetooth RFCOMM → head-unit hotspot → mDNS → iAP2/AirPlay.
- For detailed protocol basis, see [docs/PROTOCOL-NOTES.md](https://github.com/shaonialife/cardeck/blob/HEAD/docs/PROTOCOL-NOTES.md).

## Download and install

**Recommended: GitHub Release** (download directly; includes SHA-256 and signing fingerprint):

AI coding bills come in two types, and mixing them up easily leads to the wrong choice:

| Billing type | How you pay | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| **Plan-based** (Coding Plan / membership) | Monthly fee for a fixed quota; stops or throttles once used up | Coding steadily every day, with a capped budget |
| **Pay-as-you-go** (API) | Billed per token, pay for what you use | Occasional use, or embedding a model into your own product |

So this is split into three tables: **Domestic plans**, **Overseas plans**, and **API unit prices**, plus a **value-for-money ranking** calculated from real benchmark data.

> (for the history of the positioning, see issue #6463 / for the brand rename, see issue #6525).

| **Product name** | 观星台 |

| **Users** | Merchant administrators and staff, end customers, workshop workers |

| **Deployment** | Multi-tenant SaaS (tenant-level data isolation, merchant onboarding vetted automatically by AI) |

This repository is **not** a 'generic industry AI customer service template': the default industry model is soft furnishings / curtains, and industry terminology, material calculation rules, and production processes all have executable sources of truth (see the 'Documentation' section).

- **Dual agents** — 米宝 (consumer-facing, LangGraph) + 黄金策 (business-facing), driven by a tool and Skill registry
